question: What is the main feature of neoplastic diseases?

options.B: Sudden loss of normal blood circulation
options.C: Rapid healing of damaged body tissues
options.D: Permanent shrinkage of major internal organs

explanation: Neoplasms involve abnormal cells multiplying without the body's normal regulatory controls. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T12#GNS321_U1_T12_h1)

question: Why do community health nurses place a strong focus on cancer prevention?

options.A: Neoplastic diseases are strictly contagious through casual physical contact
options.B: Treatment options are always completely free in government hospitals
options.C: Early detection completely eliminates the need for any follow-up care
options.D: Prevention significantly reduces overall disease burden and death rates

explanation: Stopping cancer early or preventing it altogether saves lives and lessens the impact on healthcare systems. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T12#GNS321_U1_T12_h1)

question: Which prevention level includes routine screening tests like Pap smears?
explanation: Screening aims to detect disease early before symptoms appear, which defines secondary prevention. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T12#GNS321_U1_T12_h2)

question: A nurse teaches a client how to do regular breast self-examinations. Which prevention tier does this belong to?
explanation: Self-examinations and screenings catch health issues early, making them part of secondary prevention. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T12#GNS321_U1_T12_h2)

question: Administering the hepatitis B vaccine to infants is an example of which type of prevention?
explanation: Vaccines stop infections that can lead to cancer later in life, acting before disease starts. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T12#GNS321_U1_T12_h3)

question: What is the main goal of primary cancer prevention counseling?

options.B: Minimizing exposure to environmental and lifestyle risk factors
options.C: Detecting small tumors before they cause pain
options.D: Providing comfort measures for terminal cancer patients

explanation: Primary prevention stops the disease process by reducing exposure to things that cause cancer. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T12#GNS321_U1_T12_h3)

question: What is the main goal of secondary cancer prevention programs?

options.A: Preventing healthy individuals from encountering carcinogens
options.C: Detecting cancer early when treatment is most effective
options.D: Curing late-stage disease using advanced surgery

explanation: Early detection finds tumors at an early, manageable stage to improve survival outcomes. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T12#GNS321_U1_T12_h4)

question: A client asks why a screening test is recommended when they feel fine. What is the best nursing response?

options.A: Doctors require everyone to complete these tests annually
options.B: Screenings find abnormal changes before symptoms or pain begin
options.C: It proves your immune system is completely free of infection
options.D: Healthy people have a higher risk of developing sudden tumors

explanation: Screening tests identify early cellular changes before clinical symptoms appear. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T12#GNS321_U1_T12_h4)

question: When does tertiary prevention typically begin in a client's care timeline?

options.A: After a confirmed diagnosis and initial treatment
options.B: Prior to administering routine childhood immunizations
options.C: Before exposure to known environmental carcinogens
options.D: During routine community health screening outreaches

explanation: Tertiary prevention focuses on rehabilitation and managing complications after a disease has been diagnosed. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T12#GNS321_U1_T12_h5)

question: A nurse teaches arm exercises to a client recovering from a mastectomy to prevent lymphedema. What type of prevention is this?
explanation: Managing post-treatment complications and supporting rehabilitation falls under tertiary prevention. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T12#GNS321_U1_T12_h5)

question: Why is genetic counseling recommended for individuals with a strong family history of cancer?

options.A: To replace the need for routine physical examinations
options.B: To cure existing genetic anomalies through diet
options.C: To guarantee the patient will never develop a tumor
options.D: To identify inherited risks and guide personal screening plans

explanation: Genetic counseling helps high-risk individuals understand their inherited risks and plan appropriate health monitoring. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T12#GNS321_U1_T12_h6)

question: Which nursing action best supports effective patient education regarding cancer prevention?

options.B: Handing out lengthy research journals without talking
options.C: Using complex medical jargon and Latin terms
options.D: Using simple language suited to the client's understanding

explanation: Clear communication ensures clients actually understand risk factors and follow preventive advice. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T12#GNS321_U1_T12_h6)

question: How does community-level nursing advocacy help reduce the rates of neoplastic diseases?

options.A: By manufacturing affordable chemotherapy drugs locally
options.B: By pushing for public policies that restrict exposure to carcinogens
options.C: By performing complex surgical tumor removals in rural clinics
options.D: By diagnosing hereditary gene mutations without labs

explanation: Advocacy involves changing laws and environments to protect entire communities from cancer-causing agents. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T12#GNS321_U1_T12_h7)

question: Which activity is a direct example of a nurse engaging in community advocacy for cancer prevention?

options.A: Prescribing targeted drug therapies in a clinic
options.B: Participating in public campaigns to promote smoke-free public spaces
options.C: Performing routine microscope tissue checks in a lab
options.D: Discharging a client following uncomplicated surgery

explanation: Advocacy involves public health promotion and policy changes that protect populations from health risks. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T12#GNS321_U1_T12_h7)
